answer: Proof of Personhood using verifiable biometrics creates a basalt foundation for identity. By requiring an agent to generate a unique plume of cryptographic proofs tied to physical reality, the system renders mass identity replication computationally infeasible. An attacker seeking to flood the network must incur the steep cost of fabricating thousands of distinct human signatures, a task as difficult as composing a perfect sonnet by random chance, ensuring that influence remains tied to singular entities.
